speaker: Unknown
en: Collectively, you know, we started with this kind of gray mush in our head.
zh: 总的来说，你知道，我们一开始脑子里都是这种灰色的糊状物。

speaker: Unknown
en: We somehow started out knowing nothing at all and somehow discovered like everything that humans know today was like this process of collective discovery, like of languages and technology and science and mathematics and
zh: 我们不知怎的从一无所知开始，然后不知怎地发现了——就像今天人类所知的一切都是这样一个集体发现的过程，像是语言、技术、科学和数学，以及

speaker: Unknown
en: All the rest of it, you know, everything we learned, we discovered it for ourselves.
zh: 所有其他东西，你知道，我们学到的一切，都是我们自己发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's an incredible thing that no one has cracked yet in AI.
zh: 而这是一件令人难以置信的事情，目前在 AI 领域还没有人破解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to me, that is the essence of what it will take to get to superintelligence, like a system that can just keep learning and discovering knowledge forever.
zh: 所以对我来说，这就是达到超级智能所需要的东西的本质——就像一个能够永远不断学习、不断发现知识的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm thrilled to have Dave Silver and Lese Espeholt with us, two of the co-founders of Ineffable Intelligence.
zh: 我很高兴 Dave Silver 和 Lese Espeholt 能和我们一起，他们是 Ineffable Intelligence 的两位联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great name, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句，这个名字起得真好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fun fact, Dave, you were the first person I cold emailed to come on Training Data when we started the show 100-ish episodes ago.
zh: 有个趣事，Dave，大约在一百多集之前我们创办这档节目的时候，你是我冷邮件邀请来上 Training Data 的第一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like a full circle moment to finally have you on the show.
zh: 现在终于能请到你上节目，感觉像是一个圆满的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you for joining us.
zh: 所以感谢你加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dave, let's start with you.
zh: Dave，从你开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your 2009 PhD was on reinforcement learning applied to the devilishly difficult game of Go.
zh: 你 2009 年的博士论文是关于将强化学习应用于围棋这个极其困难的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You demonstrated for the world for the first time that superhuman...
zh: 你首次向世界展示了超越人类的……

speaker: Unknown
en: In one domain, machine intelligence was possible.
zh: 在一个领域内，机器智能是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you were really the figure that inspired the entire current generation of reinforcement learning and deep learning researchers.
zh: 而且我认为你真的是激励了整个当前这一代强化学习和深度学习研究者的关键人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so thank you for your contributions to where the field is.
zh: 所以感谢你为这个领域的现状所做的贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, thinking back to that point in time, what did you learn?
zh: 我很好奇，回想那个时间点，你学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you have conviction on?
zh: 你当时有什么样的信念？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what has remained the same and what has changed as AI has changed over the last five years or so?
zh: 在过去五年左右 AI 的变化中，哪些保持不变，哪些发生了变化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you and pleasure to be here and I'm glad I finally made it after these hundred episodes.
zh: 好的，谢谢你，很高兴来到这里，我很高兴在这上百集之后终于来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a pleasure to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I suppose I always had this conviction starting my PhD and going into the game of Go that the right approach to solve AI was through learning from experience, through systems that discovered things for themselves that were
zh: 所以我想，从我读博士、进入围棋领域开始，我就一直有这样的信念：解决 AI 的正确方法是通过从经验中学习，通过那些自己发现事物的系统，它们

speaker: Unknown
en: Learning through reinforcement learning to get better and better and better and that that would be the thing which would lead to the emergence of intelligence and ultimately super intelligence.
zh: 通过强化学习来变得越来越好、越来越好，而这将导致智能的涌现，并最终达到超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I suppose we were able to show that in the game of Go, but it's a conviction that has held true throughout my career.
zh: 所以我想我们能够在围棋中展示这一点，但这是一个在我整个职业生涯中一直成立的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here we are now applying that conviction, ineffable, trying to show that indeed superintelligence can emerge all the way through systems that learn from experience.
zh: 现在，我们正在 Ineffable 应用这个信念，试图证明超级智能确实可以完全通过从经验中学习的系统而涌现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in terms of things which are different, although we are not pursuing the human data path that the LLM world has pursued,
zh: 至于不同的方面，虽然我们没有追求 LLM 世界所走的人类数据路线，

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think there's lots of interesting lessons to learn from that.
zh: 我确实认为从那条路线中可以学到很多有趣的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: In particular, it was definitely a surprise to me how a system that was trained on a massive amount of data could then be very quickly fine-tuned on a very small amount of data to kind of completely change its behavior.
zh: 特别是，一个在海量数据上训练的系统，随后能在非常少量的数据上被快速微调，从而彻底改变其行为，这对我来说绝对是一个惊喜。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was something which I think was something which sort of changed my mindset in terms of, you know, just suggesting that if you get things at the right scale, that a lot of things which seem like incredibly hard or like they might be very slow, that once you've kind of experienced enough data, that after that, the things that were slow can become very fast.
zh: 我认为这件事在某种程度上改变了我的思维方式，就是说，如果你把事情做到合适的规模，很多看起来极其困难、或者可能非常缓慢的事情，一旦你经历了足够多的数据，之后，那些原本缓慢的事情就可以变得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a lesson that wasn't obvious to me in advance until it happened.
zh: 我认为这是一个在它发生之前对我来说并不明显的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to come back to that later.
zh: 我们稍后会回到这个话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could have run this program inside DeepMind where, you know, could have probably had more access to compute than just about anybody.
zh: 你本来可以在 DeepMind 内部运行这个项目，你知道，你拥有的算力资源可能比几乎任何人都多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You decided the right thing to do was to start a new lab.
zh: 你却决定正确的做法是创办一个新实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why'd you do that?
zh: 你为什么这么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, look, first of all, I had a fantastic time at DeepMind.
zh: 你看，首先，我在 DeepMind 度过了一段非常美好的时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: I loved my years there.
zh: 我热爱在那里度过的那些年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have a huge amount of respect for the people there and still got on with them very well.
zh: 我对那里的人非常尊重，至今和他们相处得也很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the end of the day, I have a really strong belief about how we can go beyond where we are today with AI and all the way to superintelligence.
zh: 但归根结底，我有一个非常坚定的信念，关于我们如何能超越今天 AI 的水平，一路达到超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the path that I believe in doesn't actually go through LLM-based products as an intermediate point.
zh: 而我所相信的这条路径，实际上并不以基于 LLM 的产品作为中间站。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I really thought about that, I thought about it really hard.
zh: 当我认真思考这一点时，我非常深入地思考了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I realized that I felt that so passionately that this deserved to be more than just the corner of an organization that's focused on LLM-based products.
zh: 我意识到，我对这件事怀着如此强烈的热情，以至于它值得拥有比一个专注于基于 LLM 产品的组织的某个角落更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: and deserve to be represented by an elite AI lab that really just gives this approach its all and represents it 100%.
zh: 它值得由一个精英 AI 实验室来代表，这个实验室真正地为这条路线全力以赴，100% 地代表它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once I realized that, it felt very natural to create this company.
zh: 一旦我意识到这一点，创建这家公司就感觉很自然了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I suppose another way to look at it is that the world already has tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands of really talented researchers all pursuing exactly the same approach, like really just kind of doubling down on LLMs with pre-training, post-training, coding, and that kind of LLM path.
zh: 我想另一种看待它的方式是，这个世界上已经有数万、甚至数十万非常有才华的研究者在追求完全相同的路线，就是真的只是在 LLM 上加倍下注，做预训练、后训练、编程，以及那种 LLM 路线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I going to be the 100,001 person that's pursuing that approach?
zh: 我要成为追求那条路线的第一万零一个人吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the most effective use of my time and my energy?
zh: 那是对我的时间和精力最有效的利用吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the end, I realized that there's this other lamppost that right now no one is looking under and where if I actually put my effort there, there's a much higher chance of really having a massive impact on the field.
zh: 最终，我意识到还有另一根路灯柱，现在没有人往它下面看，而如果我真正把我的努力放在那里，就有大得多的机会真正对这个领域产生巨大的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if this works, it's going to change the whole of AI.
zh: 因为如果这成功了，它将改变整个 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that kind of realization also meant that this was something which just means that it's the best way to have impact upon the field through this approach.
zh: 所以我觉得这种认识也意味着，这件事就是通过这条路径对整个领域产生影响的最佳方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus, you had a company name that couldn't go to waste.
zh: 再加上，你还有一个不能浪费掉的公司名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to say where the mind's called Ineffable?
zh: 你想说说为什么公司名叫 Ineffable 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I suppose that the name Ineffable, it came from this idea that there's really just knowledge could be
zh: 那么 Ineffable 这个名字，我想它来自这样一个想法：知识真的是可以——

speaker: Unknown
en: So incredible, like the things which superintelligence will one day discover, like this knowledge is going to be so unbelievable, incredible, and it's going to be something which is profoundly amazing and perhaps so profound that we can't even express it in human language.
zh: 非常不可思议，就像超级智能有一天会发现的东西，这种知识将会令人难以置信、不可思议，它会是极其惊人的东西，也许深刻到我们甚至无法用人类语言来表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so really it's like in line with this other path that doesn't go through human language-based approaches, but instead
zh: 所以这真的与另一条不通过基于人类语言的方法的路径相一致，而是

speaker: Unknown
en: Build systems that discover things for themselves and has the possibility to discover knowledge that's unbelievably profound and ultimately ineffable.
zh: 构建能自己发现事物的系统，并有可能发现极其深刻、最终不可言喻(ineffable)的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I should say there was also a secret second reason that we used, which was that, you know, this idea, it really has to work.
zh: 我应该说，我们用它还有一个秘密的第二原因，那就是，你知道，这个想法，它真的必须成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you really just double down on learning from experience, it's an approach that just has to work.
zh: 就是说，如果你真的押注于从经验中学习，这是一个必须会成功的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you could say that it can't possibly F up.
zh: 所以你可以说它不可能搞砸。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's ineffable.
zh: 所以它就是 ineffable(in- 是否定前缀，而 F up 是搞砸)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there you go.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the secret reason as well.
zh: 这就是那个秘密原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Best lab name.
zh: 最好的实验室名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lese, what about you?
zh: Lese,你呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You were at Google.
zh: 你之前在 Google。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were in a different group than Dave in the deep learning group at DeepMind.
zh: 你和 Dave 不在同一个组，你在 DeepMind 的深度学习组。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you spent years scaling up reinforcement learning on GPUs.
zh: 而且你花了好几年在 GPU 上扩展强化学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: What made you decide to leave DeepMind?
zh: 是什么让你决定离开 DeepMind 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what drew you to co-found Ineffable?
zh: 又是什么吸引你来共同创立 Ineffable 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I joined DeepMind in January 15.
zh: 我是 2015 年 1 月加入 DeepMind 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, I started working a bit with Dave around 16, where I was doing this work on scaling up reinforcement learning.
zh: 实际上，我在 16 年左右开始和 Dave 有一些合作，当时我在做扩展强化学习方面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as you said, I was part of the deep learning team, and he was leading a reinforcement learning team.
zh: 所以正如你所说，我是深度学习团队的一员，而他当时在领导一个强化学习团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we were working on an internal project together.
zh: 但我们一起做的一个内部项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually left DeepMind twice.
zh: 其实我离开过 DeepMind 两次。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I left DeepMind in summer 18 and went to like Google Brain.
zh: 我在 18 年夏天离开 DeepMind，去了 Google Brain。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then eventually Google Brain and DeepMind merged and then I was like back again.
zh: 后来 Google Brain 和 DeepMind 合并了，然后我又回来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the end of the day, I left DeepMind again like a year before Dave left.
zh: 但最终，我又在 Dave 离开大约一年前离开了 DeepMind。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first time I heard about it was actually through one of our eventual investors.
zh: 而我第一次听说这件事，实际上是通过我们后来的一个投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like reaching out to me, asking what I thought about Dave.
zh: 他联系我，问我觉得 Dave 这个人怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, my first reaction was, damn, I missed out on an opportunity.
zh: 我的第一反应是，该死，我错过了一个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I should have reached out to him.
zh: 我本应该主动联系他的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I recall Dave as more often than not being one of the smartest people in the room.
zh: 但在我印象中，Dave 更多时候都是房间里最聪明的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And shortly after that, seeing for that investor, they actually reached out to me.
zh: 在那之后不久，看到那位投资人，他们实际上又主动联系了我。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I really love to work with Dave.
zh: 所以我真的很想和 Dave 一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew Wojtek and Chris from back in the day and I thought the team was great and I also thought it was amazing to have an opportunity like this in Europe.
zh: 我从很早以前就认识 Wojtek 和 Chris，我觉得这个团队很棒，而且我也觉得在欧洲能有这样一个机会太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be said as well.
zh: 这里也应该说一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: We worked together on some of the early approaches to combining reinforcement learning with deep learning and trying to scale things up.
zh: 我们曾一起合作过一些把强化学习和深度学习结合起来的早期方法，并尝试把规模做大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it should be said that Lasse, who, by the way, is very modest, but he actually worked on some of the original approaches that were the first attempts to actually scale up reinforcement learning and show that it could be done at large scale and like ways to parallelize reinforcement learning and ways to kind of build out architectures that were scalable.
zh: 应该说明的是，Lasse——顺便说一句，他非常谦虚——他实际上做了一些最初的方法，是最早真正尝试扩展强化学习、证明它可以在大规模上实现的工作，比如并行化强化学习的方法，以及构建可扩展架构的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look today at the way the field's gone, like actually all of the ideas that people use today kind of sort of hail back to that original work that Lasse did back in the day.
zh: 如果你看看今天这个领域的发展方向，其实人们今天使用的所有想法，基本上都可以追溯到 Lasse 当年做的那些原创工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where all the roots come from of scaled up RL.
zh: 规模化 RL 的所有根源都来自那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he was the first to figure it out.
zh: 所以他是第一个想明白的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wonderful.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should have you guys introduce each other instead of you.
zh: 我们应该让你们俩互相介绍,而不是由你来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're both too humble to brag about yourselves.
zh: 你们俩都太谦虚了,不好意思夸自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, let's talk about Ineffable and what you're building.
zh: 好,我们来聊聊 Ineffable 以及你们在做的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a beautiful mission statement as a company.
zh: 你们公司有一份很美的使命宣言。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to build a super learner and make first contact with super intelligence.
zh: 你们要构建一个超级学习者,并与超级智能进行第一次接触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you define both of those things for us?
zh: 你能为我们定义一下这两个概念吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is a super learner and what does making first contact look like?
zh: 什么是超级学习者?第一次接触又是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so to me as super learner, it's something which is, it's got incredible capacity both in its depth of what it can learn and in its breadth.
zh: 是的,对我来说,超级学习者是这样一种东西:它在学习的深度和广度上都具有惊人的容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the depth dimension, it should be something that can start from not knowing anything at all and can go all the way through to discovering things that go way beyond what humans know.
zh: 在深度这个维度上,它应该能从完全一无所知开始,一路走到发现远远超越人类已知的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So an analogy to this would be the way that human collectively, you know, we started with this kind of gray mush in our head.
zh: 打个比方,就像人类集体那样,你知道,我们一开始脑子里就是一团灰色糊状物。

speaker: Unknown
en: We somehow started out knowing nothing at all and somehow discovered like everything that humans know today was like this process of collective discovery, like of languages and technology and science and mathematics.
zh: 我们不知怎么就 starting out 一无所知,然后不知怎么发现了——人类今天所知的一切,就是这样一个集体发现的过程,比如语言、技术、科学和数学。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the rest of it, you know, everything we learned, we discovered it for ourselves.
zh: 其余的一切,你知道,我们学到的一切,都是我们自己发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't that someone came down and gave us like a blueprint of how this should work.
zh: 并不是有人从天而降,给了我们一份关于这一切应该如何运作的蓝图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it wasn't that someone came down and gave like a trillion element data set of like, oh, this is what these things should look like.
zh: 也不是有人从天而降,给了一个一万亿条目的数据集,说“哦,这些东西应该长这样”。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually figured it out for ourselves.
zh: 我们实际上是完全靠自己搞明白的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's an incredible thing that no one has cracked yet in AI.
zh: 而这是一件了不起的事,AI 领域还没有人破解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to me, that is the essence of what it will take to get to super intelligence, like a system that can just keep learning and discovering knowledge forever.
zh: 所以对我来说,那就是通往超级智能的关键所在——一个能够永远持续学习和发现知识的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the second element is breadth, that we want something which can do this incredible discovery from all the way to incredible things, and it should be possible to drop it into any stream of experience.
zh: 第二个要素是广度,我们想要一个能够做到这种惊人发现的东西——从零一直到发现惊人的东西——而且它应该可以被打入任何一条经验流中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whether it's like a simulated world or a digital world or a physical world, whatever it's dropped into, it should be something that can just learn and learn and learn.
zh: 无论是模拟世界、数字世界还是物理世界,无论它被放进哪里,它都应该能够不停地学、学、学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the dream.
zh: 这就是那个梦想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if we crack this, then to me, it gives rise to a super intelligence that will be like encountering magic.
zh: 我认为如果我们破解了这一点,那么对我来说,它将催生一种超级智能,那会像是遇见魔法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be something which is so profoundly amazing that it will be able to do wonderful things.
zh: 它将是如此深刻地令人惊叹的东西,以至于它能够做出奇妙的事情。
